cardCatalog.answerEn: the Spanish abbreviation for the September 11, 2001 attacks
cardCatalog.noteEn: Spanish commonly names major dated events with the day number and the month initial. 11-S corresponds to English 9/11 because Spanish puts the day before the month.

cardCatalog.promptEs: gripe porcina · pánico desinformado en Twitter
cardCatalog.answerEn: The 2009 H1N1 outbreak was widely called ‘swine flu.’ Twitter's then-new real-time search made it easy to watch rumors, fear, and wildly mistaken self-diagnoses spread alongside genuine news.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The strip turns a live search page into a rapid sample of online panic: unrelated injuries, conspiracy claims, and impossible precautions are all attributed to the same outbreak.

cardCatalog.promptEs: 4chan y la cultura de imágenes en Internet
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the title text thank 4chan in a joke about stored funny images?
cardCatalog.answerEn: 4chan is an anonymous online discussion site built around posted images, and it helped popularize many internet memes—images or jokes that people repeatedly copy and remix. The joke treats a large saved collection of funny images as newly valuable wealth.
cardCatalog.noteEn: This cultural reference explains why the title text imagines a 4chan user becoming successful when image collections become the basis of monetary worth.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a spectrum showing which wavelengths a substance absorbs
cardCatalog.noteEn: When light passes through or reflects from material, particular wavelengths can be removed. The missing or weakened bands form an absorption spectrum and can help identify the material.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the long chain of computing layers make the cat-video punchline funny?
cardCatalog.answerEn: A huge, intricate stack of hardware and software work is reduced to the viewer's simple wish to watch a cat jump into a box and fall.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The chain moves from processor cycles through an operating-system kernel and compatibility layers to a browser, renderer, plug-in object, and video frames. Calling the viewer a god reverses the perspective: these complex layers serve an ordinary human request, even though the human does not directly control their details.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Why do the two workplaces react so differently to the same programming breakthrough?
cardCatalog.answerEn: The joke contrasts academic incentives to publish and teach a discovery with a company's narrow interest in whether its immediate software task now works.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The hidden breakthrough is treated as potentially important research in the academic branch, while the business branch evaluates it only as routine performance and compatibility work. The official title text sharpens the joke by suggesting that major theoretical discoveries may remain buried inside ordinary engineering code.

cardCatalog.promptEs: campos ordenados por pureza · ciencias aplicadas · matemáticas
cardCatalog.answerEn: the comic ranks academic fields by how abstract or theoretical they appear
cardCatalog.noteEn: Each field dismisses the one to its left as merely an applied form of itself. Mathematics is drawn farthest from practical application, which makes the distance itself part of the joke.

cardCatalog.promptEs: hobby · falso experto · disciplinas · segundos y minutos
cardCatalog.answerEn: the speaker tests how long graduate students in different fields take to notice that he is bluffing
cardCatalog.noteEn: Each panel gives an obviously ill-informed contribution and records the detection time. The literary-criticism group remains unconvinced only after eight papers and two books, which is the final escalation of the joke.

cardCatalog.promptEs: función de Ackermann con el número de Graham
cardCatalog.answerEn: an intentionally absurd computation involving extraordinarily fast-growing quantities
cardCatalog.noteEn: The Ackermann function grows extremely quickly even from modest inputs, while Graham's number is already unimaginably large. Using Graham's number as both inputs makes the written calculation comically impossible to carry out, which explains the mathematician's reaction.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Mortality tables summarize death rates by age or group; actuaries use them to estimate life expectancy and financial risk.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The tables describe probabilities across populations, not exact death dates for particular people. Turning them into precise predictions about named people's deaths exaggerates what the statistics can do and makes the calculation deliberately morbid.

cardCatalog.promptEs: distancia mayor · aire más rápido · presión menor · del revés
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the upside-down-flight question expose a problem with this explanation of lift?
cardCatalog.answerEn: The explanation assumes that air split by a wing must reunite at the trailing edge at the same time, but air has no such equal-transit-time requirement.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Different airflow speeds and pressures do matter for lift, but the common story that air over the longer curved surface must hurry to meet the air below is false. Lift depends on the complete flow around the wing, including its shape, circulation, and angle of attack. Aircraft can produce lift while inverted by using an appropriate angle of attack, so upside-down flight is a useful counterexample to the oversimplified story.

cardCatalog.promptEs: selección de asiento · diagrama del avión · clic en la cabina
cardCatalog.questionEn: What visual mistake creates the joke?
cardCatalog.answerEn: The passenger treats the cockpit drawn on an airline seat map as a selectable seat, so clicking it puts her in the pilot's position.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Real airline diagrams show the aircraft around the passenger seats but do not make the cockpit selectable. The final panel turns the interface click into a literal assignment to fly the plane. The title text extends the same absurd interface rule to the wing.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What is Dijkstra's algorithm?
cardCatalog.answerEn: an algorithm for finding shortest paths through a graph whose edge costs are nonnegative
cardCatalog.noteEn: It repeatedly expands the not-yet-finished point with the lowest known total cost. Unlike A*, it does not use an estimate of the remaining distance; the contrast supplies the technical content of the answer in the scene.

cardCatalog.answerEn: an early internet meme based on awkward English from the game Zero Wing
cardCatalog.noteEn: The best-known line is “All your base are belong to us.” “What you say!!” comes from the same badly translated game opening. The meme spread widely online around 2000–2001 and later became a marker of early-web nostalgia.

cardCatalog.promptEs: reordenar el alfabeto · junto a tu hermana
cardCatalog.answerEn: a twist on the familiar alphabet pickup line about putting “U and I” together
cardCatalog.noteEn: The stock English line uses the letter names U and I as the words “you” and “I.” This joke breaks the expected romantic ending by choosing the listener's sister instead.

cardCatalog.promptEs: hormigas · feromonas · búsqueda de vida inteligente
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why do the ants' pheromone trails mirror a human search for intelligent life?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Ants communicate largely through chemical trails, so they imagine that any intelligent beings should leave pheromone messages across nearby tiles. Their search repeats human reasoning about detectable extraterrestrial signals at an absurd ant-sized scale.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The caption adds another reversal: the ants are themselves the newly intelligent civilization doing the searching, while humans remain outside the signals they know how to detect.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a real Python Easter egg used as a visual joke
cardCatalog.noteEn: Python's antigravity module opens this xkcd comic in a web browser when imported.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What marketing language turns the description of the CEO into a joke?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Apple product presentations often emphasize devices as exceptionally thin and light; the speaker applies that product language to a person.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Steve Jobs was Apple's CEO and delivered its prominent keynote presentations. The comic turns his reported weight loss into a grim parody of a product unveiling.

cardCatalog.promptEs: índices de arrays desde cero o desde uno
cardCatalog.answerEn: different systems number an array's first item as either 0 or 1
cardCatalog.noteEn: Programming languages and algorithms use indexing conventions to label positions. Mixing zero-based and one-based conventions makes the same index point to different items.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the final comment undermine the criticism of the speakers?
cardCatalog.answerEn: The supposed audio expert demands high fidelity while relying on heavily compressed sources and an even lower-quality phone connection.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Audiophiles value accurate sound reproduction. The speaker mocks cheap equipment, yet listens to low-bitrate video rips; the call's still lower bitrate then becomes the excuse for withholding the punchline. The mismatch between claimed standards and actual listening conditions drives the joke.

example.es: Un audiófilo comparó dos grabaciones con distinta compresión.
example.en: An audiophile compared two recordings with different compression.

cardCatalog.answerEn: the comic's fictional narrow blood-alcohol range in which programming ability suddenly peaks
cardCatalog.noteEn: The name refers to Microsoft executive Steve Ballmer. The joke presents a precise alcohol optimum as if it were a documented scientific effect, then treats Windows ME's poor reputation as evidence of an uncontrolled attempt to exploit it.

cardCatalog.promptEs: orquídea · abeja extinta · pintura de una flor
cardCatalog.answerEn: an orchid preserving a vanished bee's appearance as a living memory
cardCatalog.noteEn: Some bee orchids evolved flowers that resemble female bees. The comic turns one self-pollinating orchid into a poignant memorial: even after the pollinating bee has disappeared, the flower's inherited shape still reflects how a plant once ‘saw’ that animal through evolution. Calling it a painting by a dying flower makes the biological relationship feel like art and remembrance.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Bell y Watson · primer mensaje telefónico
cardCatalog.answerEn: Alexander Graham Bell sent the first successfully transmitted intelligible telephone message to his assistant Thomas Watson in 1876.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The comic compares an inaugural message through TCMP with Bell calling Watson during the early telephone experiment.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What is a binary fraction, and why do values such as 1/2 or 3/4 fit?
cardCatalog.answerEn: A binary fraction has a denominator that is a power of two, such as 2, 4, 8, or 16.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The denominator is the bottom number in a fraction. Powers of two are made by repeatedly multiplying by two: 2, 4, 8, 16, and so on. That makes 1/2, 1/4, 3/4, and 7/8 binary fractions, while 1/3 is not.

example.es: La fracción tres octavos es binaria.
example.en: The fraction three eighths is binary.

cardCatalog.noteEn: The setup echoes the famous Bond-villain exchange in Goldfinger: Bond tries to keep talking his way out of a death trap, while the villain coolly says that death—not cooperation—is the expected outcome. The technical grammar argument is another delaying tactic.

cardCatalog.answerEn: A boot sector is a small disk area that contains information used when a computer starts.
cardCatalog.noteEn: A computer reads boot information before the operating system is fully running. Replacing that information with an ordinary message can stop startup and produce an error such as “Operating system not found,” which is the technical premise of the joke.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Braille and printed lettering can encode different messages on the same sign.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The joke relies on many sighted readers being unable to check the raised-dot text. A sign can therefore look ordinary in print while its Braille carries a private, hostile message.

cardCatalog.promptEs: informe de error aplicado al razonamiento humano
cardCatalog.answerEn: treating a flaw in human reasoning as if it were a software bug
cardCatalog.noteEn: A software user files a bug report so a defect can be fixed. The metaphor applies that technical workflow to an undesirable feature of the human mind.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Yo soy el que soy · compañero R2-D2
cardCatalog.questionEn: What two stories are being combined in the joke?
cardCatalog.answerEn: The visible scene merges the burning-bush declaration from Exodus with an implied C-3PO-style introduction of R2-D2.
cardCatalog.noteEn: In Exodus, God speaks to Moses from a burning bush and identifies himself with an ‘I am’ declaration and the lineage of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The comic then introduces visible R2-D2 as the speaker's companion and gives him electronic sounds. That points toward C-3PO, R2-D2's usual Star Wars companion and a robot built for languages and etiquette, even though C-3PO is never printed or drawn. The official title text reinforces the implication by asking about Bocce, a language C-3PO claims to speak; its droid-like LO-M can also be read as an echo of Elohim, a Hebrew name for God.

cardCatalog.promptEs: idea antigua · empresa rica · solicitar una parte · formulario retroactivo
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the business-idea department turn the speaker's complaint into a joke?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It treats a vague old remark as if it were formal evidence that entitles someone to a retroactive share of a company's profits.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The speaker first makes the familiar claim that a company got rich from an idea he had years earlier. The next panels imagine an official form accepting hearsay, an approximate date, a self-selected percentage, and a mailing address, followed by an implausibly immediate cash delivery.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What is A* search?
cardCatalog.answerEn: a pathfinding algorithm that combines the cost already traveled with an estimate of the cost still remaining
cardCatalog.noteEn: A* usually keeps many possible routes in memory while choosing which one looks most promising. That memory demand is the issue tested in the training scene.

cardCatalog.answerEn: the idea that a very small change can lead to much larger later differences in a chaotic system
cardCatalog.noteEn: The phrase is associated with weather and chaos theory. The comic literalizes it by treating one butterfly wingbeat as a disturbance that can be controlled precisely through the atmosphere.

cardCatalog.promptEs: C, ensamblador y Python · nivel de abstracción
cardCatalog.answerEn: C and assembly expose more low-level computer details, while Python handles more of those details for the programmer
cardCatalog.noteEn: Lower-level languages can demand more manual work but also reveal how the machine operates. The comic compares the relief of using a powered skateboard with moving to Python, then jokes that the tedious work in C or assembly might build programming skill and personal character.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a simple substitution cipher that shifts every letter by the same fixed number of positions
cardCatalog.noteEn: The method is associated with Julius Caesar. Because there are very few possible shifts, it is easy to test every key; calling a modern operating system vulnerable to it is intentionally absurd.

cardCatalog.promptEs: tecnología · consecuencias · opinión formada · usa esta frase
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why can the displayed warning about a new technology sound insightful in almost any situation?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It is deliberately vague, so listeners can supply whichever technological danger already worries them and credit the speaker with addressing it.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The upper statement recommends pausing to consider the consequences of giving a technology too much prominence, but it names no concrete consequence. The lower caption presents that broad warning as a reusable line. The Spanish title text explains that the listener mentally fills in their own alarm, making the speaker seem perceptive without having offered a specific analysis.

cardCatalog.promptEs: banderas · fronteras · servidor de capturar la bandera
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the final complaint reinterpret the diplomatic speech?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Capture the flag is a team game in which players enter opposing territory, take a flag, and return it to their base. The solemn kingdoms, borders, embassies, flags, and peace appeal are revealed as role-play on a badly designed game server.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The title text continues the game logic with a rebel collecting a row of flags and returning to base for an enormous score.

cardCatalog.promptEs: fuerza centrípeta · fuerza centrífuga · sistema en rotación
cardCatalog.answerEn: Centripetal force points inward; centrifugal force is the outward apparent force used in a rotating frame of reference.
cardCatalog.noteEn: A frame of reference is the viewpoint and coordinate system used to describe motion. From a non-rotating frame, an inward net force keeps an object moving in a circle. In a coordinate system that rotates with the object, adding an outward centrifugal term lets Newton's laws keep their familiar form. The disagreement is therefore about the chosen frame, which is the physics behind the argument.

cardCatalog.promptEs: portal fantástico · volver a casa · fingir que no sucedió
cardCatalog.answerEn: the joke follows a children's-fantasy triumph with the hero's bleak problem of returning to ordinary life
cardCatalog.noteEn: The familiar fantasy arc gives an insecure young person a magical mission, victory, and confidence, then sends him home. The last panel undercuts that empowerment: he expects decades of hiding an experience nobody else can verify.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What mathematical process is shown, and where does the joke come from?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It is the Collatz process: halve an even positive integer, or triple an odd one and add one, then repeat; the joke replaces a mathematical conclusion with friends eventually avoiding the obsessive hand calculation.
cardCatalog.noteEn: In the prompt, ÷ means divide, × means multiply, + means add, and the centered dots separate the main ideas. The Collatz conjecture says that repeatedly applying those two rules to any positive integer will eventually reach 1, though no general proof is known. The diagram traces many values into 1 while a person calculates by hand. The caption's final consequence is deliberately social rather than mathematical, and the title text extends the joke by calling obsessive manual use of any rules a ‘Strong Collatz Conjecture.’

cardCatalog.promptEs: test de visión combinado · número 42 · sinestesia · daltonismo
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does this single number picture claim to test two unrelated kinds of perception at once?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It combines an Ishihara-style color-vision plate with a number whose large shapes are themselves made from many smaller numbers.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Ishihara plates normally use colored dots to test color discrimination. Here the large 4 is drawn mainly from small 2s, the large 2 mainly from small 4s, and the surrounding field from other digits. The caption jokingly diagnoses color blindness if only one large figure is seen and synesthesia if the viewer treats the small numbers as creating the larger forms. The title text extends the mock diagnosis with diplopia and myopia under still more contrived viewing conditions.

cardCatalog.promptEs: interés compuesto · diez años · fuerza mágica
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does checking the investment result undercut the opening claim?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Compounding produces growth, but a low rate over ten years does not turn the starting sum into a spectacular fortune.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Compound interest grows exponentially because past interest joins the balance. Even so, two percent annually changes 1000 dollars to only about 1219 dollars after ten years with annual compounding; the comic prints 1279 dollars, but either result is modest rather than magical. The title text jokes about a quotation often attributed to Einstein and about treating scientists' party remarks as financial advice.

cardCatalog.answerEn: the tendency to favor evidence that supports what one already believes
cardCatalog.noteEn: Confirmation bias can make people seek, remember, or interpret information in ways that protect an existing belief while discounting contrary evidence.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Why do the characters develop elaborate judgments about nearly identical images?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Sustained attention creates expertise and a finer internal scale, even when the subject initially seems shallow or arbitrary.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The joke begins with a claim that careful attention reveals a whole world in any subject. An artificial year-long exposure to near-identical sandwich images then produces confident aesthetic distinctions, parodying both genuine expertise and snobbery.

example.es: Con práctica, una persona distingue matices que antes parecían iguales.
example.en: With practice, a person distinguishes nuances that once seemed identical.

cardCatalog.questionEn: How does the flowchart turn an attempt to cook into a repeating cycle?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Each attempt produces leftovers, delayed takeout meals, and discarded food before the desire to cook returns.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The arrows trace a self-defeating routine: ingredients are bought and partly cooked, pizza replaces the leftovers, the remaining food spoils over progressively longer delays, and the months-later arrow returns to the original resolution. The structure makes procrastination itself the recipe.

example.es: El diagrama muestra un ciclo que vuelve al principio.
example.en: The diagram shows a cycle that returns to the beginning.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Neighboring traffic lights can be timed as one network so that vehicle flows reach each intersection at manageable moments.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Traffic engineers model arrival patterns and queue lengths when choosing signal timings. Shortening one red phase in isolation can send traffic into a downstream queue or block another movement, so a locally shorter wait can produce worse network-wide congestion.
Two things changing together does not by itself show that one caused the other.

cardCatalog.promptEs: cambio de bit por un rayo cósmico
cardCatalog.answerEn: energetic radiation can disturb electronics and accidentally change a stored bit
cardCatalog.noteEn: Cosmic rays can contribute to rare hardware errors called bit flips. The absurd step in the comic is focusing one through the atmosphere so that it strikes a chosen drive platter and changes exactly the desired bit.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a safety-style counter sign that reports how long it has been since an incident
cardCatalog.noteEn: Workplaces often display the number of days since the last accident or another unwanted event. This sign is self-referential: it counts the days since someone reset the sign itself, even though resetting is also how its displayed count would normally be updated.

cardCatalog.promptEs: láser principal de la Estrella de la Muerte
cardCatalog.answerEn: the planet-destroying superlaser from Star Wars
cardCatalog.noteEn: The Death Star is a fictional space station whose main weapon concentrates energy into a destructive beam. The chart jokingly assigns that beam a precise spectral band.

cardCatalog.promptEs: fiasco de Debian-OpenSSL · agujeros de seguridad · sistemas vulnerables
cardCatalog.answerEn: the comic turns a real Debian OpenSSL weak-key incident into a list of absurd security flaws in other operating systems
cardCatalog.noteEn: Debian's 2008 OpenSSL vulnerability made cryptographic keys predictable and affected SSH keys, matching the title text about a blacklisted key. The left panels joke that essential safeguards were commented out; the table then invents vulnerabilities based on stereotypes, fantasy references, and software reputations.

cardCatalog.answerEn: deconstruction is a literary and philosophical approach that examines unstable meanings and oppositions within texts
cardCatalog.noteEn: The panel imitates dense theoretical language by claiming that deconstruction cannot be separated from either the text or the self. The title text extends the joke by pointing readers to a difficult encyclopedia article on the topic.

cardCatalog.promptEs: error · un resultado · hilo · sin respuesta · DenverCoder9
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the old unanswered thread feel like contact with a lost person?
cardCatalog.answerEn: A highly specific search finds one old post from someone with the same problem, but the thread contains no solution or later trace of its author.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The emotional joke treats an abandoned technical-help thread like an ancient message. The official title text imagines a prominent, editable summary that future visitors could update with whatever has been learned.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What makes derivado a calculus pun?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Derivado can call an idea derivative or unoriginal, while calculus studies derivatives, called derivadas in Spanish.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The Spanish forms are close rather than identical: derivado uses the masculine singular adjective form with the neuter demonstrative eso, while the mathematical noun is feminine, la derivada. The sunglasses and title-text scream frame the pun as a CSI: Miami-style one-liner.

cardCatalog.answerEn: the Spanish release title of Die Hard
cardCatalog.noteEn: The title literally refers to a “jungle of glass,” echoing the first film's skyscraper setting. Later entries are numbered under the same Spanish series title; La jungla de cristal 4 is Live Free or Die Hard.

cardCatalog.promptEs: datos digitales · copia exacta · captura degradada
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the final reposted screenshot undermine the claim about permanent digital data?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Exact bit-for-bit copying is possible, but the visibly degraded screenshot has been transformed, recompressed, and stripped of context rather than preserved as the same original file.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Digital storage does not guarantee that people keep and transmit an unchanged source. The final image accumulates interface chrome, watermarks, blur, and a repost-site logo, visually contrasting mathematical copying fidelity with how online culture actually preserves material.

cardCatalog.answerEn: an influential computer scientist and author of The Art of Computer Programming
cardCatalog.noteEn: Knuth taught at Stanford and is a natural authority to cite about algorithms and programming conventions.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a framework that multiplies estimated factors to approximate how many extraterrestrial civilizations might communicate in the Milky Way
cardCatalog.noteEn: Astronomer Frank Drake introduced the framework in 1961. Its factors concern stars, planets, life, intelligence, communication, and how long detectable civilizations last; their uncertain values make the result an estimate, not a measured count.

cardCatalog.promptEs: factor B_s en esta parodia de la ecuación de Drake
cardCatalog.answerEn: the comic's invented “bullshit” factor: how much of Drake's speculation someone is willing to accept
cardCatalog.noteEn: B_s is not part of the real Drake equation. The comic turns skepticism about uncertain inputs into one more fake multiplier, making the amount of accepted nonsense determine the answer.
The title makes an ordinary internet argument sound like an urgent moral obligation.
Python checks and associates value types at runtime.

cardCatalog.promptEs: el este y el oeste como regiones culturales
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why can “the East” lie west of someone while “the West” lies east of them?
cardCatalog.answerEn: These are conventional cultural and geographic labels, not directions measured from the current observer.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The labels grew from a Europe-centered view: East Asia became ‘the East,’ while Europe and societies historically grouped with it became ‘the West.’ From North America, traveling toward East Asia can mean going west across the Pacific, while traveling toward Europe can mean going east across the Atlantic. That mismatch creates the joke.

example.es: Desde California, Japón queda al oeste.
example.en: From California, Japan lies to the west.

cardCatalog.promptEs: valoraciones de compradores en un mercado por internet
cardCatalog.answerEn: Online marketplaces let buyers leave public ratings and written reviews about sellers and purchases.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The joke treats an absurdly dangerous shipment as one occasional bad transaction. The unhappy buyer leaves a negative review, while the title points out that many positive ratings could still hide rare disasters.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What “economic argument” is the comic using, and what makes the table funny?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It argues that a genuinely useful phenomenon should attract profit-seeking organizations; the unchecked paranormal claims contrast with accepted physics that already has practical uses.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The table pairs each claim with a lucrative or strategic use. Relativity and quantum electrodynamics get checkmarks because they support real technologies, while the claimed paranormal effects do not. This is a skeptical rule of thumb, not a formal proof. The title-text joke adds an important distinction: companies can still profit by selling a belief to customers even when the claimed effect itself does not work.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Einstein, la relatividad y la oficina de patentes suiza
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does a Swiss patent office belong in a joke about developing relativity?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Albert Einstein worked at the Swiss Federal Patent Office in Bern while developing the ideas behind special relativity.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Einstein held the patent-office job from 1902 to 1909 and published his special-relativity paper in 1905. References to relativity, a patent office, and Switzerland therefore point to that famous part of his biography.

cardCatalog.answerEn: the complete range of electromagnetic radiation, ordered by wavelength or frequency
cardCatalog.noteEn: Radio waves, microwaves, visible light, ultraviolet light, X-rays, and gamma rays are different portions of the same spectrum. Shorter wavelength corresponds to higher frequency.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Why can a parenthetical statement ending in an emoticon look ambiguous?
cardCatalog.answerEn: One closing parenthesis can look like both the smile's mouth and the end of the parenthetical text; adding another clarifies the structure but can make the face look odd.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The two rejected versions trade grammatical clarity against visual balance. The joke treats this tiny punctuation problem as an urgent topic for a prestigious talk.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a fictional electromagnetic-pulse weapon meant to disable electronics
cardCatalog.noteEn: PEM abbreviates pulso electromagnético, the Spanish term for EMP. A strong electromagnetic pulse can disrupt or damage electronic equipment; the comic turns that idea into a portable enforcement weapon.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the exchange about Ent-women turn into an awkward joke?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It treats the missing Entwives from The Lord of the Rings as though ordinary men might have the same epic explanation for not having women around.
cardCatalog.noteEn: In Tolkien's stories, the tree-like Ents have long been separated from the Entwives, whose fate is unknown. The comic translates that group as ENT-MUJERES and gives their disappearance an ancient war context. The follow-up “same story” absurdly borrows that legend as a relationship excuse, prompting the others to reject the comparison.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a triangle with three equal sides and three equal 60-degree angles
cardCatalog.noteEn: Because all three sides and angles match, an equilateral triangle is symmetric around its center. That symmetry matters in distance and path problems.

cardCatalog.answerEn: the single resistance that would have the same electrical behavior between two terminals as the whole network
cardCatalog.noteEn: A network of many resistors can sometimes be represented, from two chosen connection points, by one resistance that produces the same relationship between voltage and current. Finding that value simplifies the network without claiming that its internal layout is the same.

example.es: Calculamos la resistencia equivalente entre A y B.
example.en: We calculate the equivalent resistance between A and B.

cardCatalog.answerEn: The speaker claims to have outgrown obsessive science-fiction fandom, then immediately shows the same obsessive behavior toward politics.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The named books are from the Star Wars expanded universe, while Firefly and Battlestar Galactica are other science-fiction series. Ron Paul's supporters were highly visible online during the 2008 U.S. presidential campaign. The title text completes the joke by mixing his currency views with Star Wars's New Republic and Corusca gems.

cardCatalog.questionEn: How does the comic replace the usual magic of fantasy weapons with inconvenient material science?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Each supposedly exotic sword property has a mundane scientific cause, and the final weapon turns radiation exposure into a role-playing-game stat bonus.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Fantasy stories often give named blades supernatural origins, a blue glow near orcs, and numerical bonuses. Here antimony makes one sword brittle, actinium makes another glow constantly through radioactivity, and its '+2' applies to cancer risk rather than combat ability. The title text extends the joke by imagining a meteorite blade that is merely gravel held in a sword shape.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What makes the soul-bargain scene a parody of a software agreement?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Mephistopheles traditionally bargains for Faust's soul; the comic makes him lose that leverage to an end-user software license agreement.
cardCatalog.noteEn: In the Faust legend, Mephistopheles offers knowledge or power in exchange for Faust's soul. E.U.L.A. is the English abbreviation for End User License Agreement, the terms a software user accepts. The sign turns those routine terms into a prior contract that blocks the demon's negotiation.

cardCatalog.answerEn: the number sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8… in which each later number is the sum of the previous two
cardCatalog.noteEn: Starting with 1 and 1, add them to get 2; add 1 and 2 to get 3; then 2 and 3 to get 5. The repeated touches in the comic follow those group sizes, which is why the character recognizes the pattern.

cardCatalog.promptEs: águila · nido · agentes · frases en clave
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does an ordinary field observation prompt an urgent spy-style response?
cardCatalog.answerEn: A literal report about an eagle resembles the kind of coded phrase used in spy fiction, so the radio listener treats it as secret-agent traffic.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The caption reveals a hobby of following field biologists and deliberately treating their ordinary observations as code phrases. The title text reverses the setup by imagining an animal trainer helping secret agents when real events are impossible to describe over the radio without sounding coded.

cardCatalog.promptEs: dos años · siete años · diez años · quince años
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the strip revisit scenes separated by two, seven, ten, and fifteen years?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It presents a long cancer-survival retrospective, moving from treatment and uncertainty toward fifteen years without a recurrence.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The grayscale panels reprise earlier stages of diagnosis, treatment, recurrence anxiety, and milestones. The newer scenes add ordinary shared life, aging, and care. The final fifteen-year marker makes survival itself—not a conventional punch line—the emotional culmination.

cardCatalog.answerEn: “First post” is a deliberately low-effort internet comment whose main purpose is to claim the first comment slot rather than contribute to the discussion.
cardCatalog.noteEn: It can appear as “first,” “first post,” or an exaggerated or deliberately misspelled variant. The cliché is commonly associated with trolling because it seeks attention without adding useful content.

cardCatalog.promptEs: ancho fijo · texto monoespaciado · líneas alineadas
cardCatalog.answerEn: fixed-width text gives every character the same horizontal width
cardCatalog.noteEn: In a monospaced or fixed-width font, narrow letters and wide letters occupy equal space. Text strings with the same number of characters therefore have the same visual length, which is useful for code, terminals, and aligned text art.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What were Flash browser games?
cardCatalog.answerEn: They were games made with Adobe Flash that ran inside a web browser, usually through a small browser add-on called a plug-in.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Flash supported animation, sound, and interaction, so it became a common platform for quick web games before modern browser technologies replaced it. Adobe ended support for Flash Player in 2020.

example.es: Muchos juegos Flash se abrían desde una página web.
example.en: Many Flash games opened from a web page.

cardCatalog.promptEs: diagrama de flujo · pasos y ramas sí/no
cardCatalog.questionEn: How does a flowchart represent a process with decisions?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It connects steps with arrows and sends a decision along different labeled branches, often ‘yes’ and ‘no.’
cardCatalog.noteEn: A flowchart makes the possible routes through a process visible. Rectangles commonly show steps, diamonds show decisions, and branch labels determine which path to follow. The comic turns those conventions into a self-referential test of whether the reader can follow the chart.

example.es: El diagrama de flujo separa las respuestas sí y no.
example.en: The flowchart separates the yes and no answers.

cardCatalog.promptEs: coche volador · teléfono · videojuego · videollamada · estrellarse
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the reply argue that a flying car would be unsafe despite impressive modern technology?
cardCatalog.answerEn: The phone already combines shopping, books, 3D games, and video calls, but the user's distraction by that same device would make a flying car dangerous.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The complaint treats flying cars as the missing sign of the future while ignoring capabilities that already arrived in a handheld device. The final warning turns that wonder into a safety problem: typing or gaming while piloting would add airborne consequences to familiar distracted-driving behavior.

example.es: La tecnología nueva no elimina el riesgo de usarla sin atención.
example.en: New technology does not remove the risk of using it inattentively.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What does a Fourier transform reveal about changing data?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It rewrites a changing signal as a collection of repeating frequencies. A strong peak can reveal a prominent repeating cycle.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The title text extends the graphing joke by claiming that a Fourier analysis finds a one-month pattern in the relationship data.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Benjamín Franklin · signos de la carga eléctrica
cardCatalog.answerEn: Benjamin Franklin introduced the positive and negative labels for electric charge. By the modern convention, glass rubbed with silk is positive; the visitor wants those labels reversed.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The labels predate the discovery of electrons. Conventional current follows the direction assigned to positive charge, while electrons in metal move the other way, so the signs can feel backward in circuit work. The joke is that an electrical engineer uses the time machine to change this convention instead of preventing a robot apocalypse.

cardCatalog.answerEn: The joke treats freedom as the unsettling ability to make a wildly unexpected choice at any moment.
cardCatalog.noteEn: One speaker argues that ordinary self-imposed rules hide a vast field of possible life-changing actions. The sudden punch demonstrates that freedom while also proving why another person's options can be frightening; the final response celebrates precisely that failure to predict it.

cardCatalog.promptEs: campo de fútbol · guepardo · ballena azul
cardCatalog.answerEn: a monster built from familiar size, speed, weight, age, and area comparisons
cardCatalog.noteEn: Popular explanations often make huge measurements easier to picture by comparing them with football fields, cheetahs, blue whales, young children, stadiums, or familiar territories. The comic personifies that habit as a literal monster whose destructive acts merely generate more of the same comparisons.

cardCatalog.promptEs: productividad · coeficiente de rozamiento · silla de oficina
cardCatalog.questionEn: What scientific convention turns the office-chair graph into a joke?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Physics commonly uses µ for a friction coefficient, while the graph treats chair friction as though it controlled workplace productivity.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Lower friction lets a swivel chair spin more freely. The curve gives that amusement a mock productivity optimum, while the title text extends the joke: as µ approaches zero, other people join chair-spinning contests and the group's productivity becomes negative.

cardCatalog.promptEs: fulgurita: arena fundida por un rayo
cardCatalog.answerEn: A lightning strike can melt and fuse sand into glassy formations called fulgurites.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The device routes lightning through collected sand, turning a real geological effect into an elaborate glass-necklace joke.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Gary Gygax co-created the tabletop role-playing game Dungeons & Dragons.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Paladins, adventuring groups, and extensive rulebooks are familiar parts of Dungeons & Dragons. The comic imagines that Gygax has turned Death's simple game for his soul into a long tabletop campaign, and the title text memorializes him shortly after his death in 2008.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What is a campana de Gauss?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It is a bell-shaped curve representing a normal distribution: values near the center are common and values in the tails are rare.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Gauss is the mathematician whose name is attached to this model. Referring to a point at the extreme of the bell invokes one of the curve's rare tails.

cardCatalog.promptEs: pasar la sal · sistema · condimentos arbitrarios · ahorrar tiempo
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the promised time-saving system make the exchange absurd?
cardCatalog.answerEn: A simple request to pass the salt is delayed while the listener builds a general-purpose condiment-passing system.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The joke contrasts solving one immediate task with overengineering a reusable solution. The official title text extends the contrast by showing how present-day thoroughness can look like poor prioritization while similar past work is praised as craftsmanship.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the enormous cost assigned to becoming Skynet matter to the joke?
cardCatalog.answerEn: A genetic algorithm searches for good candidate solutions by optimizing a fitness or cost function, so a huge cost can make an unwanted outcome extremely unattractive when the program minimizes cost.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Skynet is the hostile artificial intelligence in the Terminator stories. The code treats an AI takeover as just another outcome to penalize. The title-text warning completes the joke: if the program maximized this cost instead, the enormous number would encourage precisely that outcome.

cardCatalog.promptEs: mi casa · mapa de ejemplo de geografía
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the speaker want to live inside a textbook-style map?
cardCatalog.answerEn: The artificial example map puts nearly every major landform—and the speaker's house—conveniently together.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Geography diagrams often compress mountains, rivers, plains, islands, and other features into one implausibly tidy landscape so they can all be labeled. The joke treats that teaching diagram as a desirable real address.

cardCatalog.promptEs: corriente inducida por una tormenta solar
cardCatalog.questionEn: How can activity on the Sun produce electric current in long conductors on Earth?
cardCatalog.answerEn: A solar storm can disturb Earth's magnetic field. A changing magnetic field can induce voltage and current, especially across very long conductors such as power lines and pipelines.
cardCatalog.noteEn: This real large-scale effect is called geomagnetically induced current. The comic exaggerates it into an implausible claim that an ordinary extension cord could cause worldwide melting and fires; Earth's rotation is not the mechanism normally responsible for the storm-induced current.

cardCatalog.promptEs: El regalo de los Reyes Magos y su parodia
cardCatalog.questionEn: What literary joke is suggested by El robo de los Reyes Magos?
cardCatalog.answerEn: O. Henry's story has each partner secretly sell their own prized possession to buy a gift for the other. The parody changes the gift into theft: each person sells the other's property, and each purchase serves the seller's own plans.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The English title Theft of the Magi plays on O. Henry's The Gift of the Magi. The Spanish title makes the same contrast between regalo, “gift,” and robo, “theft.”

cardCatalog.promptEs: la broma de internet que recuerda la tira
cardCatalog.answerEn: It refers to an infamous early-web shock image that people spread through deceptive links.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The characters imagine future nostalgia for an old trolling ritual: using fake profiles and a social forum to trick strangers into opening an explicit image. The title text warns readers not to search for the reference.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What does “Godwin's Law” refer to?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It is the observation that a comparison involving Hitler or the Nazis becomes increasingly likely as an online discussion grows longer.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Mike Godwin coined the observation about internet discussions. It does not forbid every historically relevant mention of Hitler or require a conversation to end; treating it that way is a common comic exaggeration.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Google Maps: imágenes y nivel de zoom
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does a Google Maps zoom message turn the romantic scene into a joke?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Map services may lack imagery at very close zoom levels; the scene treats looking deeply into a person's eyes as if it were zooming into a map.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The woman has just joined the Google Maps team. The mapping-service limitation therefore appears where a romantic revelation should be, combining her new job with the literal idea of looking deeper.

example.es: Amplía el mapa para ver la calle.
example.en: Zoom in on the map to see the street.

cardCatalog.promptEs: unirte · como · qué demonios · en realidad
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the final change of mind make the social-network exchange a joke?
cardCatalog.answerEn: The listener first resists a new service because it is described as Facebook, then suddenly realizes that a Facebook-like service was what he wanted.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Google+ launched as a social network in 2011 and was commonly compared with Facebook. The blank middle panel gives the listener time to reconsider. The official title text adds a two-sided joke: parents being hard to persuade to switch is both a disadvantage and an advantage of a new network.

cardCatalog.promptEs: GOTO y el flujo de un programa
cardCatalog.answerEn: GOTO jumps directly to a named point in code; overusing it can make a program's execution path hard to understand
cardCatalog.noteEn: Structured programming normally uses functions, loops, and conditionals to keep control flow visible. A GOTO can be useful in limited cases, but arbitrary jumps can create tangled “spaghetti code” whose execution path is difficult to reason about.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Día de la Marmota · seis semanas más de invierno
cardCatalog.answerEn: a Groundhog Day prediction that winter will last six more weeks
cardCatalog.noteEn: In the North American Groundhog Day tradition, a groundhog that sees its shadow and returns to its burrow supposedly predicts six more weeks of winter. The comic replaces the groundhog with a newborn retreating into the womb, which makes the doctor's prediction absurdly literal.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a rhythm video game whose soundtrack supplies the bands named in the comic
cardCatalog.noteEn: Players perform rock songs with a guitar-shaped controller. The joke is that apparent music knowledge can come from memorizing the game's track list rather than exploring the artists independently.

cardCatalog.answerEn: A gyroscope is a spinning device whose axis resists being reoriented and can slowly turn through precession.
cardCatalog.noteEn: A rapidly spinning rotor has angular momentum, so changing the direction of its axis produces motion that can seem counterintuitive. Precession is the gradual turning of that axis under an applied force such as gravity.
The unusual operating system derails the scripted support conversation.

cardCatalog.promptEs: regla de la mitad de la edad más siete
cardCatalog.questionEn: What is the informal “half your age plus seven” dating rule?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It claims that half a person's age plus seven is the youngest partner age that would not seem socially inappropriate.
cardCatalog.noteEn: This is a folk rule and a common joke device, not an ethical or scientific standard. It can be treated as a numerical boundary when discussing possible partners.

cardCatalog.promptEs: visión de calor de Jack Black
cardCatalog.answerEn: a reference to the unaired comedy pilot Heat Vision and Jack
cardCatalog.noteEn: Jack Black played an astronaut whose mind expanded in sunlight, and his character rode a talking motorcycle. The tiny motorcycle on the graph distinguishes this reference from Superman's literal heat vision.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Hello, World — a traditional first program
cardCatalog.noteEn: Many programming tutorials begin with the smallest program that displays a short message.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What progression do the rising curves satirize?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Each later curve represents a more self-aware complaint about hipsters, ending with a graph that complains about the whole chain and thereby adds yet another level.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The chart moves from seeing hipsters, to complaints about them, to complaints about the repeated word, and then to complaints that all such meta-commentary is the same insecure navel-gazing. The final curve says that graphs make everything worse, but that graph is itself another example. The similarly rising curves visualize an escalating loop of ironic detachment.

cardCatalog.answerEn: The scratched device reveals a reference to The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Douglas Adams's science-fiction series features an electronic guide containing vast amounts of useful travel information. A wirelessly connected e-reader resembles that fictional guide, so scratching away the Kindle branding uncovers the joke's imagined true identity.

cardCatalog.promptEs: sociedad de honor · club de la tautología
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why do the honor society and the Tautology Club form the joke?
cardCatalog.answerEn: The honor claim is circular, and the invented club repeatedly states facts that merely repeat themselves.
cardCatalog.noteEn: A tautology repeats the same idea or is true by definition. The club's membership promise says that a group with one million members will have one million members, while its first rule is simply identified as itself. The opening also mocks circular prestige: membership proves someone honorable because honorable people supposedly belong.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a guessing game in which ‘cold’ means far from the target, ‘warm’ means closer, and ‘hot’ means very close
cardCatalog.noteEn: The handheld unit gives only these proximity clues instead of turn-by-turn directions. Turning the children's guessing game into a navigation system is what makes this an intentionally cheap GPS.

cardCatalog.promptEs: entradas y salidas de la casa
cardCatalog.questionEn: How does the grid turn a house into an input-and-output joke?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Each row treats a real house input as though it could be routed to every output: sensible matches work, while mismatches scratch cars, explode houses, sicken people, or send wastewater through the wrong place.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The columns are a well, garage, power line, door, and septic tank. The rows are drinking water, cars, electricity, people, and wastewater. Green diagonal cells are the intended connections. The red cells imagine the physical result of sending each input to the wrong destination, borrowing the logic of a computing input/output matrix for household infrastructure.

cardCatalog.answerEn: A haiku is a Japanese poetic form commonly taught outside Japan as three short lines following a 5–7–5 rhythm; the comic jokes that HTML markup can satisfy both code rules and poetic form.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The title text adds that the count becomes harder when angle brackets are pronounced aloud, making the way code symbols are read part of the joke.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a made-up ice-age unit that makes projected warming visually comparable with major past climate change
cardCatalog.noteEn: The chart defines one unit as the roughly 4.5-degree global difference between the coldest part of the last ice age and a modern reference. It then places projected warming on that scale. This exposes how a few degrees of global average warming can represent a climate shift comparable in magnitude to moving out of an ice age, with radically different coastlines and polar conditions.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Why are a vacuum and zero friction central to the joke?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Physics problems often remove air resistance and friction to create simple idealized models; the comic turns those assumptions into a place where real professors have been deposited.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Ideal conditions make equations easier by eliminating forces that complicate motion. The experiment treats those textbook simplifications as a literal environment and then mocks the professors for disliking the conditions they routinely impose on imagined objects. The official title text adds that two other subjects remain lost on an infinite plane of uniform density.

cardCatalog.answerEn: indentation used to mark code structure
cardCatalog.noteEn: Python uses indentation as part of its block syntax.

cardCatalog.promptEs: sanear entradas de base de datos
cardCatalog.noteEn: The concept means validating untrusted input and, in practice, using parameterized queries.

cardCatalog.answerEn: IPv6’s original specification appeared in 1998; the joke treats an IPv6 address block as the finite supply of identities available to a nanobot swarm.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The core IPv6 specification, RFC 2460, was published in 1998. IPv4’s limited address space motivated IPv6, whose 128-bit addresses are unimaginably numerous. The comic imagines self-replicating nanobots stopping after consuming only part of Earth because their swarm was still assigned too small an IPv6 subnet and ran out of addresses.

cardCatalog.promptEs: techno · repetir · veces · muestra · segundos · obtener lo mismo
cardCatalog.answerEn: the joke compares repetitive techno with looping a very short digital music preview
cardCatalog.noteEn: The store name itself remains an excluded brand label. The humor comes from treating a short free sample as enough material to recreate a whole track by repeating it, exaggerating techno's use of repeated electronic patterns.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a reference to Independence Day, where Jeff Goldblum's character uses a PowerBook to help upload a virus to the alien mothership
cardCatalog.noteEn: The comic turns that film scene into a mock software vulnerability: merely encountering the named laptop supposedly threatens the operating system.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Testing many colors separately makes it likely that at least one will appear linked to acne by chance; highlighting only that result turns random noise into a dramatic headline.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The strip illustrates the multiple-comparisons problem, often exploited through p-hacking: repeated tests create more chances for an apparently interesting result. In the official strip, the lone green result has P<0.05, the conventional threshold used to flag statistical significance. The Spanish raster mistakenly prints P>0,05 there as well as in the other twenty panels, and this source error is preserved. The newspaper then turns the selected result into misleading 95% reliability and 5% chance claims.

cardCatalog.promptEs: tomar el juramento presidencial · un error muy conocido
cardCatalog.questionEn: What real event makes the comparison about administering a presidential oath funny?
cardCatalog.answerEn: While administering Barack Obama's first presidential oath in 2009, U.S. Chief Justice John Roberts put faithfully in the wrong place; he administered the oath again correctly the next day as a precaution.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The comic appeared days after the widely noticed mistake and compares that formal stumble with the speaker's much more awkward imagined version of the oath.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does calling this a ‘Jurassic Park’ parenting approach make the plan darkly comic?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Jurassic Park's engineered dinosaurs were supposed to depend on a supplied nutrient as a containment safeguard; the parent proposes creating a medical dependency and controlling the matching supply.
cardCatalog.noteEn: In the story, the dinosaurs' engineered lysine dependence is meant to keep them under control if they escape. Deliberately causing diabetes and then controlling access to insulin turns that fictional contingency plan into an alarming parenting policy.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a classical Sanskrit work widely known for its descriptions of sexual positions
cardCatalog.noteEn: The work covers a broader range of ideas about desire, relationships, and social life, but popular culture most often associates its name with illustrated sexual positions.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Kill Bill · tema de lucha · Battle Without Honor or Humanity
cardCatalog.answerEn: The imagined soundtrack is the dramatic track “Battle Without Honor or Humanity,” prominently used in Kill Bill.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The comic's title text names the track and jokes that, like “Ride of the Valkyries,” it makes any ordinary activity feel like a cinematic confrontation.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Klingon is a constructed fictional language from Star Trek, not a member of the Finno-Ugric language family
cardCatalog.noteEn: The Finno-Ugric branch includes real languages such as Finnish, Estonian, and Hungarian. Suggesting Klingon as another member exposes that the speaker is bluffing about linguistics.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the future punch request work like a deliberately self-hostile dead man's switch?
cardCatalog.answerEn: The speaker asks to be punched if he ever uses Klout for anything except removing himself, and he orders his friend to ignore any later attempt to cancel the instruction.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Klout was a service that assigned public social-influence scores. The speaker treats using it as shameful enough to justify a future punishment. A dead man's switch normally triggers when its operator stops actively preventing it; the title text jokingly applies that idea to a standing anti-Klout instruction that the speaker's future self cannot safely revoke, because every retraction must be ignored.

cardCatalog.promptEs: problema de la mochila · suma exacta
cardCatalog.answerEn: select a subset of available items that obeys a limit or hits an exact target
cardCatalog.noteEn: The classic knapsack problem chooses items with weights and values under a capacity limit. Asking which menu prices add to one exact total is more specifically the closely related subset-sum problem. The decision versions are NP-complete, so the restaurant request hides a computationally difficult search inside an ordinary order.

cardCatalog.promptEs: bata de laboratorio · autoridad médica aparente
cardCatalog.answerEn: A lab coat is only clothing; buying one does not provide medical training or make absurd anatomical claims reliable.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The joke lets a confidently dressed speaker give a nonsensical account of childbirth, then undercuts that apparent authority by pointing out that anyone can simply buy a lab coat.

cardCatalog.promptEs: casa de LEGO · piezas · ordenación · donante de órganos
cardCatalog.answerEn: a joke about whether identity survives when the same material is rearranged
cardCatalog.noteEn: The father distinguishes a LEGO house from the plastic pieces that compose it: once its particular arrangement is gone, the house no longer exists as that object. The later organ-donor choice extends the same unsettling question to a person, whose organs may remain even though their arrangement as one living person does not.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Natural cosmic rays already produce very energetic particle collisions, a comparison used to argue that starting the Large Hadron Collider would not create a new planet-destroying danger.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The opening fear imagines the collider's startup ending life on Earth. The reply invokes cosmic rays, which have struck Earth naturally for an extremely long time, and the physics student treats the alleged catastrophe mostly as an excuse for a party. That contrast supplies the scientific setup for the joke.

cardCatalog.promptEs: extrapolar · ayer · hoy · más de cincuenta maridos
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why is the graph's prediction absurd?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It draws a straight trend through only two observations—zero husbands yesterday and one today—and extends that line far beyond the observed time. Two points always determine a line, but they provide almost no evidence that the real situation will continue linearly.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The title text repeats the same error with pregnancy: it projects a rapidly growing count into a later trimester as though every short-term change must continue unchanged.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Linux y el antivirus de consumo
cardCatalog.answerEn: Retail antivirus products have historically been marketed mainly to Windows users, so a Linux user may reject that particular sales pitch.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The stunt exaggerates that confidence for the joke. Linux systems can still face malware and other security threats; using Linux does not make a computer automatically invulnerable.

cardCatalog.promptEs: puerto · hardware · software · proyecto · soporte · Linux
cardCatalog.answerEn: a Linux user treats an implanted physical computer port as useful because a future software project might eventually make it work
cardCatalog.noteEn: The patient knows that merely wiring a port to nerves cannot make the brain control devices. He still wants the hardware installed and trusts that an open-source software project will eventually add support. The surgeon recognizes this optimistic hardware-first attitude as characteristic of a Linux user; the official title text extends the joke with a Vista-Ready sticker.

cardCatalog.promptEs: de instalar Linux a compilar el kernel
cardCatalog.answerEn: The comic compresses a Linux learner's rapid progress from a basic installation request to reading Unix manuals, switching distributions, and building a custom kernel.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Xorg is a display system; Ubuntu, Debian, and Gentoo are Linux distributions; and the kernel is the operating system's core. Moving through those topics in a few weeks signals increasingly advanced and obsessive involvement. The final warning copies the tone of a parental public-service announcement for the joke.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Linux · miles de procesadores · vídeo Flash fluido
cardCatalog.questionEn: What contrast creates the joke about the patch's supported features?
cardCatalog.answerEn: The patch supports an unusually specialized machine with thousands of processors, yet the user still cannot smoothly play ordinary full-screen Flash video. The developer celebrates impressive large-scale engineering while dismissing the everyday feature the other person actually wants.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Linux is an operating-system family. Flash was a widely used web-media platform when the comic appeared in 2009, and smooth video playback depended on practical graphics, driver, and software support rather than merely accepting a huge processor count.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Apache y Linux frente a Menú Inicio, Mis Documentos y AOL
cardCatalog.answerEn: Apache can run as a web server on Linux, while Start and My Documents are Windows interface names and AOL Keywords belonged to AOL. Those steps do not address the caller's Linux server problem.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The Black Hat character deliberately gives obsolete, mismatched consumer-computer instructions. The growing mismatch is the central support-call joke.

cardCatalog.promptEs: baterías de litio · usos comerciales · envejecer hacia atrás
cardCatalog.questionEn: What development makes the reverse-aging wish funny?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Lithium batteries moved from specialized medical uses into phones and then inexpensive remote-controlled aircraft. The speaker wishes he could become younger as the increasingly appealing toys become cheap and widely available.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The title text confirms that the speaker compulsively buys inexpensive remote-controlled aircraft.

cardCatalog.promptEs: lotería · prueba viviente · sesgo de supervivencia
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why is the lottery winner's motivational advice misleading?
cardCatalog.answerEn: The visible winner treats persistence as proof while the many persistent losers are absent from the story.
cardCatalog.noteEn: This is survivorship bias: attention goes to the rare successful case that can give a talk, not to the much larger set of people who followed the same strategy and lost. The money bags make the speaker's luck visible, while the caption identifies the reasoning error.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the comic treat an apparently obvious fact as a daily opportunity?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Because people continually reach the age at which they can encounter any familiar fact for the first time, so sharing it can be more enjoyable than mocking them for not already knowing it.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The comic estimates that roughly 1,300 people in Spain encounter a given piece of common knowledge for the first time each day. The product demonstration turns the calculation into a concrete moment of delighted discovery.

cardCatalog.answerEn: the joke disguises simply firing a gun as one of MacGyver's elaborate improvised solutions
cardCatalog.noteEn: MacGyver is a television hero known for escaping danger with ingenious devices assembled from whatever is available, and for avoiding conventional weapons. The joke's technical chain describes the ordinary operation of a pistol in grand detail, making his supposed invention both unusually direct and comically lazy.

cardCatalog.promptEs: ataque de intermediario en una red
cardCatalog.answerEn: an attacker secretly intercepts traffic between two endpoints and may block or alter it before forwarding it
cardCatalog.noteEn: VPN and SSH encryption are designed to resist this kind of interference. The joke exaggerates Mrs. Roberts's skill: she detects new tunnels immediately, disrupts connections, and even changes requested pages and the live TCP data stream.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Margarine is greasy, so fetching it implies an immediate plan to use it as an improvised sexual lubricant.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The original English comic names Crisco, a brand of vegetable shortening, for the same implication. The Spanish version substitutes margarina. That unexpectedly practical response is the final escalation of the joke.

cardCatalog.answerEn: references Memento, a film whose color scenes run in reverse chronological order
cardCatalog.noteEn: Christopher Nolan's Memento follows a man with severe short-term memory loss. One sequence of scenes moves backward in time, so viewers repeatedly learn what happened just before the scene they have seen.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Merlín · T. H. White · vida hacia atrás
cardCatalog.answerEn: references T. H. White's Merlin, who experiences time backward
cardCatalog.noteEn: In The Once and Future King, T. H. White portrays Merlin as living backward through time. He knows events that are still in other people's future while his own past becomes their future.

cardCatalog.promptEs: premio al visitante número 100.000.000 · anuncio parpadeante en la web
cardCatalog.answerEn: Early web advertisements often falsely claimed that the viewer was a numbered visitor who had won a valuable prize. Flashing text was meant to attract clicks, not prove that a real prize existed.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The speakers treat the familiar fake promotion literally: they bought a car for the supposed winner and assume the winner simply missed the flashing notice. The official title text extends the joke to other implausible advertising claims that legitimate businesses would struggle to distinguish from spam.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Edad Moderna · modernismo · mid-century modern · posmodernidad · moderno
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why is the timeline's repeated use of “modern” funny?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Several different eras and movements keep names meaning “modern,” so an old label for the present survives after it is no longer current.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The chart places the conventional Edad Moderna, modernism, mid-century modern, postmodernity, and a present-day “modern” segment along one chronology. Each label arose in a different historical or stylistic context, but their overlapping claims to modernity make the terminology look self-contradictory. The caption jokingly credits historians with this accumulation.

cardCatalog.answerEn: the conspiracy claim that the Apollo Moon landings did not happen
cardCatalog.noteEn: Moon-landing denial claims that NASA staged the Apollo landings despite extensive physical, photographic, technical, and independent evidence for the missions.

cardCatalog.answerEn: charts that turn a movie's character interactions into paths through time
cardCatalog.noteEn: Each line follows a character, and nearby lines show characters sharing a scene. The joke contrasts stories that form readable patterns with Primer, whose famously tangled time-travel plot becomes an almost indecipherable knot.

cardCatalog.answerEn: the humorous rule that if something can go wrong, it will
cardCatalog.noteEn: Murphy's law is an engineering and everyday-life adage, not a scientific law. References to Murphy often personify bad luck, failure, or the unforeseen ways a design can break.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Who are the Cazadores de Mitos mentioned here?
cardCatalog.answerEn: MythBusters was a television show whose hosts tested popular claims and dramatic myths with experiments.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Cazadores de Mitos is a descriptive Spanish rendering of the show's English name. The joke suggests that inventing a frightening scientific claim would give the program another myth to investigate.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Navajo Code Talkers transmitted military messages using a sophisticated code based on the Navajo language
cardCatalog.noteEn: Their historical system was much richer than replacing binary zero and one with two spoken words. The comic's supposed extra encryption is funny because the repeated pattern remains transparently binary.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What historical rivalry do the two matching invention claims refer to?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Newton and Leibniz developed calculus in different forms. Newton worked earlier, while Leibniz published first and introduced notation that became widely used.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Historians credit the two men with independent developments, followed by a bitter dispute over priority among them and their supporters. The years in the strip are compact labels for the period of their work, not publication dates.

cardCatalog.promptEs: Nochebuena · ningún sonido · clic de un ratón
cardCatalog.answerEn: The narration parodies the famous Christmas poem commonly called 'Twas the Night Before Christmas.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The poem opens on Christmas Eve and describes a house so quiet that not even a mouse is stirring. The comic replaces that quiet animal with the click of a computer mouse, then has Santa find someone awake at three in the morning.

cardCatalog.promptEs: nombres renacentistas de las Tortugas Ninja
cardCatalog.answerEn: the four Ninja Turtles are named after Italian Renaissance artists
cardCatalog.noteEn: Leonardo, Michelangelo, Donatello, and Raphael can each evoke both a historical artist and a fictional turtle. The chart compares those two kinds of name recognition.

cardCatalog.answerEn: problems whose proposed solutions are quick to check but which have no known efficient general solver
cardCatalog.noteEn: NP-complete problems are the hardest problems in the class NP, in a precise sense: every NP problem can be efficiently translated into any NP-complete problem. If an efficient general algorithm were found for one of them, it would efficiently solve every problem in NP. No such algorithm is currently known.

cardCatalog.answerEn: octarine is the fictional eighth color of magic in Terry Pratchett's Discworld
cardCatalog.noteEn: The arrow outside the real visible colors treats this fantasy color as though it had a physical wavelength beyond violet.

cardCatalog.answerEn: OpenBSD is an operating system known for emphasizing security; the comic invents shark attacks as its absurd remaining security problem.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The worsening computer repair ends with the characters in shark-filled water. The title text pretends that 40% of OpenBSD installations cause shark attacks and calls that the system's only standing security issue.

cardCatalog.promptEs: OS X · say · sintetizador de voz por línea de comandos
cardCatalog.questionEn: What makes it possible for a Mac to speak text from the command line?
cardCatalog.answerEn: OS X includes a command named say that sends typed text to the system speech synthesizer.
cardCatalog.noteEn: A terminal command is text entered into a command-line interface. Running say followed by words makes the Mac read those words aloud; command-line tools can also adjust settings such as volume. The joke depends on remote access to the Mac and this built-in speech tool.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Papyrus is a widely available display typeface that many designers criticize as overused and visually clichéd.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Its faux-handwritten look appears in many informal signs and themed designs, which has made it a recurring target of typography jokes. Giving a carefully meant card set in Papyrus is therefore framed as an irritant to a typography enthusiast; the official title text adds that the narrator secretly likes the typeface and expects beautifully typeset complaints.

cardCatalog.answerEn: a joke that a portion of the spectrum is hidden under a U.S. surveillance law
cardCatalog.noteEn: The USA PATRIOT Act expanded government surveillance powers after 2001. The blacked-out band exaggerates secrecy by pretending a law can censor part of nature itself.

cardCatalog.promptEs: PERL, LISP y un paréntesis de cierre
cardCatalog.answerEn: Perl and Lisp are programming languages; Lisp represents code with many nested expressions enclosed in paired parentheses.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The comic imagines the universe as source code. The huge ) at its right edge acts like the final closing parenthesis of a Lisp program; an unmatched parenthesis can change or break the program's structure.

cardCatalog.answerEn: hypothetical motion that continues forever without an energy source
cardCatalog.noteEn: A machine that produces useful work forever without added energy would violate the laws of thermodynamics. Claims of such machines are therefore treated as impossible under established physics.

cardCatalog.promptEs: células cancerosas · placa de Petri · pistola
cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the gun undermine the claim about killing cancer cells in a dish?
cardCatalog.answerEn: Many things can kill isolated cells in a laboratory dish; that alone does not show that they are safe or useful cancer treatments in a person.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The setup warns about impressive-sounding claims that a medicine or vitamin kills cancer cells in vitro—that is, outside a living body in laboratory conditions. A gun can also destroy those cells, exposing how little the claim proves without evidence about selectivity, dosage, safety, and effects in a living organism.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Photoshop is software used to alter images, and ‘Photoshopped’ commonly means digitally manipulated.
cardCatalog.noteEn: Edited images can contain clues such as inconsistent reflections, lighting, edges, or compression artifacts. The joke treats those familiar signs of manipulation as if they could prove that physical objects in the real world had been edited too.

cardCatalog.answerEn: Pluto was classified as a dwarf planet rather than one of the Solar System's eight planets under the International Astronomical Union's 2006 definition.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The 2006 definition requires a Solar System planet to orbit the Sun, be nearly round, and have cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit. Pluto meets the first two conditions but not the third, so the IAU placed it in the distinct dwarf-planet category.

cardCatalog.answerEn: any power of one is still one
cardCatalog.noteEn: Raising one to an integer power means multiplying copies of one, so the value remains one: 1⁰, 1¹, 1², and 1³ all equal 1. A negative power also remains one because its reciprocal is 1/1.

cardCatalog.answerEn: In classical logic, accepting both a claim and its negation makes it possible to derive any claim.
cardCatalog.noteEn: P∧¬P represents a proposition P together with ‘not P,’ a direct contradiction. The principle is called explosion because unrestricted conclusions then follow. The joke treats those conclusions as a way to obtain unrelated personal facts and plans rather than merely proving propositions.

cardCatalog.questionEn: What is the improvised antenna in this comic doing?
cardCatalog.answerEn: It is a homemade directional wireless antenna made from a cylindrical snack can to reach a Wi-Fi network farther away.
cardCatalog.noteEn: The official English text calls it a “Pringles cantenna.” The joke uses that improvised antenna to reach the network across the street before the characters' own service is connected.

example.es: Una antena direccional concentra la señal.
example.en: A directional antenna concentrates the signal.

cardCatalog.questionEn: Why does the network prefix turn the campfire story into a technical horror joke?
